mainTopic: The judges who measure for the עגלה ערופה, hidden and 'floating' corpses and sheaves, and the laws of שכחה
overview: The גמרא finishes explaining how many judges go out to measure for the עגלה ערופה. It shows that the plural words ויצאו and ומדדו teach other laws: the judges go in person, and they always measure. Our משנה does not follow רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, who says the סנהדרין, the מלך and the כהן גדול must take part. רב יוסף tries to prove from the case of a זקן ממרא at בית פגי that he needs the entire סנהדרין. אביי pushes the proof aside, but a ברייתא then supports רב יוסף. Next, the גמרא shows that even the רבנן agree a hidden corpse gets no עגלה ערופה, because each פסוק is read by its own context, and it maps out the sources for the laws of שכחה. רבי ירמיה asks whether sheaves floating in the air of one's own field count as in the field, and two attempted proofs are turned aside. Finally a scholar asks אביי which of two stacked bodies to measure from, and אביי's answer begins on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי שמעון does not learn from the extra letter ו
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון does not count extra judges from the ו of ושופטיך. To him, the word means the distinguished ones among the judges.
steps.simpleTranslation: He does not learn anything from the letter ו. What is the תורה saying with 'and your judges'? It means the distinguished ones among your judges.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes explaining why רבי שמעון needs only three judges and not five like רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה counts two more judges from the ו ("and") in ושופטיך. רבי שמעון does not learn anything from that letter. So he reads שופטיך as describing which elders go out, the special ones, and not as adding more people.

keyTerms.meaning: the letter ו (meaning "and"), sometimes used to add something extra
he does not learn from it
the Merciful One, meaning the Torah
the distinguished, special ones

phrases.english: He does not learn anything from the letter vav.
phrases.notes: "He" is רבי שמעון. The vav is the "and" at the start of וְשֹׁפְטֶיךָ.

phrases.english: What is the Merciful One saying?
phrases.notes: This line and the next are both inside round brackets, so some versions leave them out.

phrases.english: The distinguished ones among your judges.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the explanation, begun before this section, of how רבי שמעון reads the פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי שמעון does not learn anything from the ו, so ושופטיך adds no judges. It only describes them as distinguished.

steps.title: Shouldn't 'go out' and 'measure' add more judges too?
steps.stepSummary: If every plural word adds two judges, then ויצאו and ומדדו should add four more. That would make nine for רבי יהודה and seven for רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if so: 'and they shall go out' means two more, and 'and they shall measure' means two more. Then for רבי יהודה there are nine here, and for רבי שמעון there are seven!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the whole method of counting judges from plural words in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both opinions count two judges from each plural word, like זקניך. But the same פסוק has two more plural verbs, ויצאו and ומדדו. If the method is consistent, each opinion should add four more judges, and nobody holds that.

keyTerms.meaning: but if so (introducing a challenge built on the previous logic)
and they shall go out
and they shall measure

phrases.english: But now, if so:
'And they shall go out' — two;
phrases.notes: דברים 21:2

phrases.english: 'And they shall measure' — two;
according to Rabbi Yehuda, there are nine here;
according to Rabbi Shimon, there are seven here!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the counting method used by both רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון.
steps.kashyaTarget: The method of learning two judges from each plural word in the פסוק
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Being consistent means ויצאו and ומדדו should each add two judges. That gives totals no one holds.

steps.title: Those words teach other laws
steps.stepSummary: ויצאו teaches that the judges must go themselves and not send agents. ומדדו teaches that they measure even when the closest city is obvious, because the measuring is itself a מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: That verse is needed for what a ברייתא teaches: 'And they shall go out' means they themselves, not their agents. 'And they shall measure' means that even if the body was found clearly next to a city, they would still measure, because it is a מצוה to measure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that ויצאו and ומדדו are already used for other lessons, so they cannot also add judges.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A word that is "used up" teaching one law is not available to teach another. ויצאו teaches that the judges must go in person. ומדדו teaches that measuring is required even when it seems pointless.

keyTerms.meaning: he needs it (for a different lesson)
as was taught in a ברייתא
their agents
clearly, plainly visible
measuring

steps.whatToRemember: ויצאו means the judges go in person, with no agents. ומדדו means they always measure, because measuring is a מצוה.

phrases.english: That verse — he needs it
for that which was taught in a baraita:
'And they shall go out' — they, and not their agents;
'And they shall measure' — that even if it was found
clearly next to the city, they would measure,
because it is a מצוה to engage in measuring.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The words are needed for other lessons
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every plural word in the פסוק adds two judges.
steps.terutzMaskana: ויצאו and ומדדו teach the laws of going in person and always measuring, so they add no judges.

steps.title: Our משנה does not follow רבי אליעזר בן יעקב
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב reads זקניך as the סנהדרין and שופטיך as the מלך and כהן גדול. Our משנה does not follow him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Our משנה is not like רבי אליעזר בן יעקב. A ברייתא teaches that רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says: 'your elders' means the סנהדרין, and 'your judges' means the king and the כהן גדול.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third opinion about who goes out to measure, and notes that our משנה disagrees with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון read זקניך and שופטיך as giving a number of judges. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב reads them as naming specific groups: the סנהדרין, and also the מלך and the כהן גדול.

keyTerms.meaning: our משנה is not in line with the opinion of...
your elders
your judges
the High Court
the High Priest

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנִיתִין דְּלָא כְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב.
phrases.english: Our mishna is not in accordance with Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov.

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: As it was taught in a baraita: Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov says:
'Your elders' — this is the Sanhedrin;

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִיתִין דְּלָא כְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב

steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, the סנהדרין, the מלך, and the כהן גדול take part in the measuring.

steps.title: Why the מלך and כהן גדול are called judges
steps.stepSummary: A פסוק in משלי calls the מלך a judge, and a פסוק in דברים connects the כהן גדול to judging.
steps.simpleTranslation: The king, as it is written: 'A king by justice establishes the land.' The כהן גדול, as it is written: 'And you shall come to the priests the Levites and to the judge who will be...'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא proves that the מלך and the כהן גדול can be called "judges", so the word שופטיך can refer to them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each person is tied to a פסוק that links him with judgment. This supports reading שופטיך as the מלך and the כהן גדול rather than as a number of ordinary judges.

keyTerms.meaning: as it is written
justice, judgment
the judge

phrases.english: A king — as it is written:
'A king by justice establishes the land';
phrases.notes: משלי 29:4

phrases.english: A High Priest — as it is written:
'And you shall come to the priests the Levites
and to the judge who shall be, etc.'
phrases.notes: דברים 17:9

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the reading in step 4 with פסוקים.
steps.raayaObject: That the מלך and the כהן גדול are called judges

steps.title: Does רבי אליעזר בן יעקב need the whole סנהדרין?
steps.stepSummary: Does רבי אליעזר בן יעקב argue only about adding the מלך and the כהן גדול, while agreeing that five or three judges from the סנהדרין are enough? Or does he require the entire סנהדרין?
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: Does רבי אליעזר בן יעקב argue only about the king and the כהן גדול, while about the סנהדרין he holds like רבי יהודה or like רבי שמעון? Or perhaps he argues about the סנהדרין too, so that the measuring needs the entire סנהדרין?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises an open question about how far רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's opinion goes. The answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It is clear that he adds the מלך and the כהן גדול. What is unclear is whether "זקניך means the סנהדרין" stands for a few members of the סנהדרין, as the others hold, or for the full court.

keyTerms.meaning: a question was asked among the scholars
he disagrees
or perhaps
the entire סנהדרין

phrases.english: A dilemma was raised before them:
Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov —
is it about the king and High Priest that he disagrees,
but regarding the Sanhedrin,

phrases.aramaic: אִי כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אִי כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן סְבִירָא לֵיהּ,

steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי אליעזר בן יעקב requires the entire סנהדרין, or only five or three of its members plus the מלך and the כהן גדול.

steps.title: רב יוסף brings the case of the זקן ממרא at בית פגי
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף quotes a ברייתא: if a זקן ממרא found the סנהדרין at בית פגי and rebelled against them there, it does not count as rebellion, because the פסוק says the place makes it count.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: Come and hear. If a rebellious elder found the judges at בית פגי and rebelled against them there, you might think his rebellion counts. The פסוק says "go up to the place," which teaches that the place is what makes it count.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף starts trying to answer the question from Step 6 by quoting a ברייתא. This step only sets up the case; the next steps will draw the proof out of it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says a זקן ממרא is only guilty if he rebels against the סנהדרין in their proper place, the לשכת הגזית. The key detail for our סוגיא is that the סנהדרין was somewhere else, at בית פגי. רב יוסף will use the fact that they left to prove something about רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.

keyTerms.meaning: A rebellious elder: a sage who rules against the סנהדרין in practice
A place outside the סנהדרין's regular meeting place
Rebellion against the ruling of the סנהדרין
The place causes it: the location is what makes the law apply

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: Come and hear:
If a rebellious elder found them at Beit Pagei
phrases.notes: אַבֵּי is a short way of saying "at the house of," so it means "at בית פגי."

phrases.english: and he rebelled against them,
one might think his rebellion should count as a rebellion.
The verse says:

phrases.english: This teaches that the place is what causes it.

steps.raayaObject: Whether רבי אליעזר בן יעקב requires the entire סנהדרין to go out for the עגלה measuring.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about a זקן ממרא who rebelled against the סנהדרין at בית פגי.

steps.title: How many judges went out to בית פגי?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how many judges were at בית פגי. If only some went, the ones still inside might agree with the elder. So it must be that all of them went out.
steps.simpleTranslation: How many went out? If you say only some of them went out, maybe the ones still inside agree with him! Rather, it is obvious that all of them went out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is building רב יוסף's proof one step at a time. It shows that the ברייתא must be talking about a case where the entire סנהדרין left.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If only part of the סנהדרין were at בית פגי, the elder's rebellion would not count for a simpler reason: the judges back home might agree with him. Since the ברייתא needed a פסוק about "the place," the case must be one where every judge was out.

keyTerms.meaning: Went out
Some of them, part of them
The ones inside
It is obvious

phrases.english: How many went out?
If you say that only some of them went out,
perhaps those who are inside
phrases.notes: He means the judges still sitting in the סנהדרין's regular place.

phrases.english: hold like him!
Rather, it is obvious that all of them went out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Analyzes the ברייתא from Step 7 to pin down the case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How many members of the סנהדרין were at בית פגי.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: All of them, because otherwise the ones inside might agree with the elder.

steps.title: Why did they leave? Not for an optional matter
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the whole סנהדרין left. It cannot be for an optional matter, because a פסוק teaches that at least twenty-three must always stay.
steps.simpleTranslation: And for what reason did they leave? If it was for an optional matter, could they all leave? But the פסוק says: "Your navel is like a round goblet, let no mixed wine be lacking." This teaches that if one of them needed to leave, he may go if twenty-three are still there, like a small סנהדרין. If not, he may not go.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps building the proof. It now asks why the whole סנהדרין went out, and rules out the idea that it was for a non-מצוה reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A פסוק in שיר השירים is read as a rule: the סנהדרין may never drop below twenty-three judges in its place. So the whole group could not leave for an optional matter. That leaves only one possibility: they went out for a מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: An optional matter, not a מצוה
A round goblet, read here as the סנהדרין's half-circle seating
A small סנהדרין of twenty-three judges

phrases.english: And for what?
If for an optional matter,
are they able to go out?
But isn't it written:
"Your navel is like a round goblet,
phrases.notes: שיר השירים 7:3. The גמרא reads this as describing the סנהדרין.

phrases.english: let no mixed wine be lacking",

if there are twenty-three there,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Since all of them left (Step 8), the גמרא asks why, and rules out an optional reason.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: For what purpose the entire סנהדרין left its place.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Not for an optional matter, since twenty-three must always remain.

steps.title: So they went for a מצוה: measuring for the calf
steps.stepSummary: So they must have left for a מצוה. רב יוסף suggests it was measuring for the עגלה ערופה, which proves that רבי אליעזר בן יעקב requires the whole סנהדרין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is obvious they went for a מצוה. Which one? Isn't it measuring for the calf, and this follows רבי אליעזר בן יעקב?
steps.whatsHappening: This is the end point of רב יוסף's proof. He names the מצוה that brought the whole סנהדרין out: measuring for the עגלה ערופה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the whole סנהדרין went out to measure, then measuring needs all seventy-one judges. That only fits רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, who says זקניך means the סנהדרין. So the answer to Step 6 would be that he requires the entire סנהדרין, not just five or three.

keyTerms.meaning: A matter of a מצוה
The measuring for the עגלה ערופה, to find the closest city

phrases.english: Rather, it is obvious that it was for a matter of a מצוה.
For what?
Is it not for the measuring of the calf,
and it follows Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the reasoning of Steps 7-9 and applies it to the question in Step 6.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי אליעזר בן יעקב requires the entire סנהדרין to go out for the measuring.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of the זקן ממרא at בית פגי, read as the whole סנהדרין going out for the עגלה measuring.

steps.title: אביי: maybe they went out to expand the city
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejects the proof. The whole סנהדרין might have gone out to add to the city or the עזרות, which a משנה says needs a court of seventy-one.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: No. Perhaps they went out to add to the city and to the courtyards. As we learned in a משנה: We do not add to the city or to the courtyards except with a court of seventy-one.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back on רב יוסף's proof. He shows there is another מצוה that could explain why the whole סנהדרין went out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף assumed the only מצוה that needs all seventy-one judges outside is the עגלה measuring. אביי points to a משנה: expanding ירושלים or the עזרות also needs the full court of seventy-one. So this ברייתא on its own does not prove anything about רבי אליעזר בן יעקב. The next step brings another ברייתא that supports רב יוסף.

keyTerms.meaning: To add to the city: expanding the holy area of ירושלים
The courtyards of the בית המקדש
The court of seventy-one, the great סנהדרין
As we learned in a משנה

steps.whatToRemember: אביי shows that רב יוסף's proof from this ברייתא is not conclusive, because the whole סנהדרין could have left for a different מצוה. The next step brings a ברייתא that supports רב יוסף.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him: No,

phrases.aramaic: דִּלְמָא לְהוֹסִיף עַל הָעִיר וְעַל הָעֲזָרוֹת.

As we learned in a mishna:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב יוסף's conclusion in Step 10 by offering another explanation of the ברייתא.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the last link of the proof: which מצוה brought the whole סנהדרין out. The earlier reasoning still stands.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the עגלה measuring is the only מצוה that brings all seventy-one judges out. Expanding the city or the עזרות also needs all seventy-one.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רב יוסף
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא names measuring for the עגלה as a case where the סנהדרין went out to בית פגי. This shows the whole סנהדרין does the measuring, just as רב יוסף said.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא agrees with רב יוסף: if the זקן ממרא found the סנהדרין at בית פגי and rebelled against them, for example when they went out to measure for the עגלה or to add to the city and the courtyards, you might think his rebellion counts. The פסוק says 'and you shall arise and go up,' which teaches that the place makes it count.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that backs up רב יוסף after אביי pushed his proof aside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי said the סנהדרין might have gone to בית פגי only to add to the city or the עזרות. This ברייתא lists measuring for the עגלה as a separate example of the full סנהדרין being out there. So measuring for the עגלה ערופה does need the whole סנהדרין, which is what רב יוסף said is the view of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.

steps.title: Does the hidden-corpse rule follow only רבי יהודה?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says a corpse hidden in a pile of stones or hanging on a tree gets no עגלה ערופה. The גמרא suggests this follows only רבי יהודה, who also excludes a hidden sheaf from שכחה, and not the Rabbis.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: if the corpse was found hidden in a pile of stones or hanging on a tree, there is no עגלה ערופה. Shall we say our משנה follows רבי יהודה and not the Rabbis? A ברייתא teaches: 'And you forget a sheaf in the field' leaves out a hidden sheaf, says רבי יהודה. The Sages say: 'in the field' comes to include a hidden sheaf.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new line of the משנה and asks whether it matches only one side of a known argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the laws of שכחה, רבי יהודה reads 'in the field' as leaving out hidden things. The Sages read the same word as including hidden things. The משנה leaves out a hidden corpse, which looks like רבי יהודה's reading, so the Rabbis would seem to disagree with our משנה.

steps.title: רב: even the רבנן agree, because context decides
steps.stepSummary: רב says the משנה can match the Rabbis too. In each place the extra word is read according to the context of its own verse.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: you can even say the משנה follows the Rabbis. Here we learn from the context of the verse, and there we learn from the context of the verse.
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers the question by saying the two cases are not the same. The next steps spell out exactly how each verse's context works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Rabbis do not have one fixed rule for what a word like 'in the field' always means. The word's job depends on what the rest of the verse already implies. So the Rabbis can include a hidden sheaf and still exclude a hidden corpse.

steps.title: In עגלה ערופה, 'in the ground' limits the law
steps.stepSummary: 'If a slain person be found' would cover a corpse found anywhere. So the extra words 'in the ground' come to leave out a hidden corpse.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'If a slain person be found,' which means wherever he is found. Then 'in the ground' comes to leave out a hidden one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the עגלה ערופה side of רב's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'found' alone would include every corpse, even a hidden one. Since the starting point is already wide, the extra words 'in the ground' can only be there to narrow it. That is why a hidden corpse is left out, even according to the Rabbis.

keyTerms.meaning: If a slain person be found
Wherever he is found

steps.title: In שכחה, 'in the field' widens the law
steps.stepSummary: Forgetting sheaves is compared to harvesting, which deals only with what is visible. So the extra words 'in the field' come to add hidden sheaves.
steps.simpleTranslation: And there we also learn from the context of the verse, as it is written: 'When you reap your harvest in your field and forget a sheaf.' Forgetting is like harvesting: just as harvesting deals with what is visible, so forgetting deals with what is visible. The Torah wrote 'in the field' to include the hidden sheaf.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the שכחה side of רב's answer and finishes the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In שכחה the starting point is narrow, because forgetting is linked to harvesting, and harvesting is done on visible grain. Since the default leaves hidden sheaves out, the extra words 'in the field' can only be there to add them. So the same kind of extra word narrows in one verse and widens in the other, and the Rabbis fully agree with our משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Similar to harvesting
With what is visible, out in the open

steps.whatToRemember: Even the Rabbis agree a hidden corpse gets no עגלה ערופה. In עגלה ערופה the default is wide, so the extra word narrows it. In שכחה the default is narrow, so the extra word widens it.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't assume an extra word in a פסוק always includes or always excludes. Here the Rabbis read similar extra words in opposite ways, because each verse starts from a different default.

steps.title: Why does רבי יהודה need a verse to leave out hidden sheaves?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יהודה: he could exclude hidden sheaves by comparing forgetting to harvesting, just like the רבנן.

steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא takes the reasoning the רבנן used in Step 16 and asks why רבי יהודה doesn't use it too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 16, the רבנן said שכחה is compared to harvesting, and harvesting only deals with what you can see. That comparison alone already leaves out hidden sheaves. So why would רבי יהודה need the extra word 'בַּשָּׂדֶה' to teach the same thing?

steps.title: Yes, רבי יהודה learns it from the harvesting comparison

steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, that is indeed so.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts the challenge instead of fighting it. רבי יהודה really does learn the rule from 'forgetting is like harvesting'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This settles where רבי יהודה gets the hidden-sheaf rule, but it opens a new problem. If the comparison does that job, then the word 'בַּשָּׂדֶה' is left without a job according to רבי יהודה.

steps.title: So what is 'בַּשָּׂדֶה' for?
steps.stepSummary: Since רבי יהודה doesn't need 'בַּשָּׂדֶה' for hidden sheaves, the גמרא asks what he uses it for.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then, why do I need 'in the field'?
steps.whatsHappening: This follows directly from Step 18: the word 'בַּשָּׂדֶה' now seems to have no purpose for רבי יהודה, so the גמרא asks what it teaches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is that the תורה doesn't use extra words for nothing. Once the hidden-sheaf rule comes from the comparison, 'בַּשָּׂדֶה' needs a new job.

steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally we think of שכחה as sheaves already cut and bundled. 'בַּשָּׂדֶה' teaches that grain still attached to the ground, which the farmer forgot to reap, also goes to the poor.

steps.title: A proof from רבי אבהו that floating sheaves in one's own field are forgotten

steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר said the exclusion applies to sheaves that floated into a friend's field. רב כהנא reads this closely: if floating into your own field were also excluded, רבי אלעזר would not have limited it to a friend's field. steps.title: If you read it that closely, resting sheaves in a friend's field would be forgotten
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: reading רבי אלעזר's words that closely would lead to an impossible result about sheaves resting in another's field.
steps.simpleTranslation: And by your reasoning: in another person's field, if they floated, yes, they are excluded, but if they are resting on the ground, no? But we need 'in your field,' and this is not his field!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that reading every word of רבי אלעזר as a strict limit leads to nonsense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'floated' were a precise condition, sheaves lying on the ground in a friend's field would still be שכחה. That cannot be, because the פסוק requires 'your field' and a friend's field is not yours. So the details in רבי אלעזר's words cannot all be read as strict limits.

steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the inference from the word 'floated' in רבי אלעזר's teaching.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Reading the details strictly would make resting sheaves in a friend's field שכחה, which goes against the requirement of 'your field.'

steps.title: 'Floated' only describes how sheaves usually get into a friend's field
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes the rejection: even resting sheaves in a friend's field are excluded, and 'floated' was said only because that is how they usually get there.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, sheaves in another person's field are excluded even if they are resting. The reason he said 'floated' is that the only way you find this case is when they floated over.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the word 'floated' as just describing the normal situation, so no proof can come from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sheaves normally reach a friend's field only by being carried through the air, so רבי אלעזר described that case. Since 'floated' is just a description and not a rule, nothing can be learned from it about floating in your own field. So this proof does not answer רבי ירמיה, and the next step tries another source.

keyTerms.meaning: And even
And the reason he said this
Because you only find this case when

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי אלעזר made 'floating' a condition. It just describes the common case, which is why the proof falls away.

phrases.english: Rather: into another's field,
even if they are resting.
And the reason he says "floated"
is that you only find this case when they floated.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: לְתוֹךְ שְׂדֵה חֲבֵירוֹ, וַאֲפִילּוּ מוּנָּחִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the rejection begun in Step 28 by explaining the word 'floated.'
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof from רבי אבהו.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: 'Floated' describes the usual way sheaves reach a friend's field and is not a legal condition.

steps.title: A ברייתא about one sheaf placed on top of another
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא: a sheaf placed on top of another and forgotten. The תנא קמא and רבי שמעון disagree about the lower sheaf.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: A sheaf that he picked up to bring to the city, and he put it on top of another sheaf and forgot it. The lower one is שכחה, and the upper one is not שכחה. רבי שמעון בן יהודה says in the name of רבי שמעון: neither one is שכחה. The lower one, because it is hidden. The upper one, because it is floating.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא makes a second try at answering רבי ירמיה by quoting a ברייתא. It is setting up the proof that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the upper sheaf is lying on another sheaf and not on the ground, so it is like sheaves 'floating' above the field. רבי שמעון calls it 'floating' and says it is not שכחה. The two opinions disagree only about the lower, hidden sheaf.

keyTerms.meaning: A sheaf of grain
A forgotten sheaf, which belongs to the poor
The lower one / the upper one
Hidden, covered up
Floating, not touching the ground

phrases.english: Come and hear:
A sheaf that he took hold of
in order to bring it to the city,
and he placed it on top of another sheaf, and forgot it:
the lower one is a forgotten sheaf,
and the upper one is not a forgotten sheaf.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Yehuda says in the name of Rabbi Shimon:
Neither of them is a forgotten sheaf:
the lower one because it is hidden,
and the upper one because it is floating.
phrases.notes: 'Floating' here means it rests on the other sheaf, not on the ground of the field.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: עוֹמֶר שֶׁהֶחְזִיק בּוֹ לְהוֹלִיכוֹ לָעִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first proof was rejected, brings a new source for רבי ירמיה's question.
steps.raayaObject: That a sheaf in the airspace of the field is not 'in the field' and so is not שכחה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about one sheaf placed on top of another.

steps.title: Everyone agrees the upper, 'floating' sheaf is not forgotten
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that both opinions agree the upper sheaf is not שכחה, which suggests that floating sheaves do not count as in the field.
steps.simpleTranslation: They only disagree about the lower sheaf. But about the upper one, everyone agrees that it is not שכחה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the proof out of the ברייתא: the upper sheaf, which is off the ground, is not שכחה according to everyone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument is only about the lower, hidden sheaf. On the upper sheaf, which sits above the field like something floating, both sides agree it is not שכחה. This points to an answer for רבי ירמיה: the airspace of a field does not count as the field.

keyTerms.meaning: They only disagree about
Everyone agrees

steps.whatToRemember: The first proof (from רבי אבהו) failed because 'floated' only described the usual case. The second proof uses a ברייתא where everyone agrees the upper, off-the-ground sheaf is not שכחה.

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא פְּלִיגִי אֶלָּא בְּתַחְתּוֹן,
phrases.english: They only disagree about the lower sheaf,
but about the upper one,
everyone agrees it is not a forgotten sheaf!

steps.triggerLanguage: עַד כָּאן לָא פְּלִיגִי אֶלָּא בְּתַחְתּוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the proof out of the ברייתא quoted in Step 30.
steps.raayaObject: Sheaves in the airspace of one's own field are not considered in the field and are not שכחה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The agreement of both opinions in the ברייתא that the upper sheaf is not שכחה.

steps.title: The upper sheaf was already acquired by the owner
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof from the ברייתא. The upper sheaf is not שכחה because the owner already took hold of it and acquired it, not because it is 'floating.'
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there: since he took hold of it, he acquired it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof from Step 31. It gives a different reason why the upper sheaf is not שכחה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 31 assumed the upper sheaf is not שכחה because it isn't touching the field. Now the גמרא says the real reason may be different. The owner already picked it up to bring it to town, so it already belongs to him. If so, the ברייתא proves nothing about floating sheaves.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different there; a standard way to reject a proof
He took hold of it
He acquired it; it became his

phrases.english: It is different there,
phrases.notes: 'There' means the ברייתא about the sheaf on top of another sheaf.

phrases.english: since he took hold of it, he acquired it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in Step 31
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the upper sheaf in the ברייתא
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The upper sheaf may be exempt because the owner already acquired it, not because it is floating

steps.title: Then why mention a sheaf on top of another?
steps.stepSummary: If the reason is that the owner acquired it, then a sheaf he put straight down on the field should also not be שכחה. So why does the ברייתא mention 'on top of another'?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why specifically on top of another? The same is true even in the field!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the explanation it just gave. If acquiring is the reason, the detail 'on top of another sheaf' seems pointless.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the new explanation, it shouldn't matter where the owner put the sheaf down. Even one placed directly on the ground would already be his. So why did the ברייתא describe the case as one sheaf on top of another?

keyTerms.meaning: If so
Why specifically this case?
On top of another (sheaf)

phrases.english: If so, why specifically
on top of another?
Even in the field as well!
phrases.notes: He means a sheaf the owner picked up and then put down right on the ground.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the explanation given in Step 32
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the upper sheaf is exempt because the owner acquired it
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If acquiring were the reason, the detail 'on top of another' would be unnecessary

steps.title: The detail is there for the lower sheaf
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא agrees that a sheaf put straight down in the field would also not be שכחה. The ברייתא mentioned 'on top of another' to teach the law of the lower sheaf.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, that is true. The ברייתא says 'on top of another' because of the lower sheaf.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It admits the point, and explains that the detail was needed for a different reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The setup of two sheaves was needed to teach the argument about the lower sheaf. The upper sheaf is not why the ברייתא chose that case. So the explanation from Step 32 still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes, that is indeed so
The lower one

phrases.english: Yes, it is indeed so,
and the reason it teaches 'on top of another'
is because of the lower one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 33
steps.terutzResolutionType: Agreeing with the point and explaining why the detail was mentioned
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The phrase 'on top of another' must be the reason the upper sheaf is exempt
steps.terutzMaskana: The phrase is there for the lower sheaf's law; the upper sheaf is exempt because it was acquired

steps.title: But the reason given was 'because it is floating'
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא itself gives the reason 'because it is floating.' That does not fit the claim that the reason is acquisition.
steps.simpleTranslation: But he said, 'because it is floating'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the explanation again, this time from the wording of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון explicitly says the upper sheaf is exempt because it 'floats.' That sounds like a reason about not touching the field, not about the owner acquiring it.

keyTerms.meaning: Floating; not resting directly on the ground
But he said; quoting a source against an explanation

phrases.english: But he said 'because it is floating'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge against the explanation of Step 32
steps.kashyaTarget: The acquisition explanation for the upper sheaf
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא's stated reason is 'floating,' not acquisition

steps.title: Read it as 'like floating'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads the ברייתא as 'because it is like floating.' The sheaf is treated as if it never left the owner's hands.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say: 'because it is like floating.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by adjusting the wording of the ברייתא slightly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Like floating' means the sheaf is treated as if it is still in the owner's hands and was never really set down. So the word 'floating' is just a picture of acquisition. The rejection of the proof from Step 32 stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Say instead; read the text this way
Like floating; as if it was never put down

phrases.english: Say: 'because it is like floating.'
phrases.notes: Just one letter is added (כְּ, 'like'). The sheaf is treated as if it's still held in the owner's hands.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 35
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Like floating' means treated as still held, which is acquisition
steps.whatToRemember: The upper-sheaf ברייתא cannot settle רבי ירמיה's question. Its upper sheaf may be exempt only because the owner already acquired it.

steps.title: אביי says he is ready for any question
steps.stepSummary: אביי declares that he is as sharp as בן עזאי was when he taught in the markets of טבריא.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: I am now like בן עזאי in the markets of טבריא.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. אביי invites questions, and the next step brings a question that is put to him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בן עזאי was famous for answering any question asked of him in public. אביי's boast opens a new question that is connected to the 'floating' idea we just saw.

keyTerms.meaning: I am hereby
The markets of טבריא

phrases.english: Abaye said: I am hereby like Ben Azzai
in the markets of Tiberias.
phrases.notes: בן עזאי would answer any question people asked him there. אביי is saying, 'Ask me anything.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: הֲרֵינִי כְּבֶן עַזַּאי בְּשׁוּקֵי טְבֶרְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new, related story
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אביי claims he can answer any question

steps.title: Two slain bodies one on top of the other
steps.stepSummary: A scholar asks אביי: if two slain bodies are found one on top of the other, which one do we measure from for the עגלה ערופה?
steps.simpleTranslation: One of the Sages said to אביי: two slain people, one on top of the other, where does one measure from?
steps.whatsHappening: A scholar takes up אביי's challenge and asks him a question about עגלה ערופה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For an עגלה ערופה, the distance is measured from the body to the nearest city. If two bodies lie stacked, and not lined up exactly, measuring from each could lead to a different city. So the question is which body counts.

keyTerms.meaning: Slain people (found murdered)
Measures (the distance to the nearest city)
The calf whose neck is broken when a murdered body is found

phrases.english: One of the Sages said to Abaye:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁנֵי חֲלָלִים זֶה עַל גַּבֵּי זֶה,
phrases.english: Two slain people, one on top of the other,
from where does one measure?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The question put to אביי after his boast
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which of two stacked bodies is used to measure for the עגלה ערופה

steps.title: The two sides: buried or floating?
steps.stepSummary: The question depends on how to view a thing lying on its own kind. Either the lower body counts as 'buried,' so we measure from the upper one. Or the upper body counts as 'floating,' so we measure from the lower one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is a thing on its own kind considered buried and not floating, so we measure from the upper one? Or perhaps a thing on its own kind is considered floating and not buried, so we measure from the lower one?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out the two sides of the scholar's question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה teaches that a buried body or a floating body does not get an עגלה ערופה. Option one: the bottom body counts as buried, so only the top one counts. Option two: the top body counts as floating, so only the bottom one counts. It is the same 'floating' idea as with the sheaves.

keyTerms.meaning: A thing in contact with its own kind
Buried; hidden
Or perhaps; introduces the other side of a question
The upper one

steps.confusionAlert: Each side makes only one of the two bodies count. Both sides agree we measure from just one body. They argue only about which one.
steps.whyThisMatters: It ties straight back to the sheaf discussion. Does something resting on top of another thing count as 'floating,' or does the thing underneath count as 'buried'?

phrases.english: Is a substance on its own kind considered buried,
and a substance on its own kind not considered floating,
and one measures from the upper one?

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִּלְמָא: מִין בְּמִינוֹ הָוֵי צָף,
phrases.english: Or perhaps: a substance on its own kind is considered floating,
and a substance on its own kind is not considered buried,
and one measures from the lower one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the two sides of the question in Step 38
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a thing on its own kind counts as buried (the lower one) or as floating (the upper one)

steps.title: Third option: measure from neither body
steps.stepSummary: The questioner adds a third possibility. A thing lying on its own kind might count as both 'buried' and 'floating' at the same time. Then neither body can be used for measuring. The גמרא then introduces אביי's reply.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or perhaps a thing lying on its own kind counts as buried, and a thing lying on its own kind also counts as floating. Then we measure neither from the lower body nor from the upper body? אביי said to him:
steps.whatsHappening: The questioner finishes his question to אביי by offering a third way to see the case. The last words, 'He said to him,' are setting up אביי's answer, which comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 39 there were two choices: the lower body is 'buried' (so we use the upper one), or the upper body is 'floating' (so we use the lower one). Here the questioner suggests that both labels could be true together. Then the lower body is disqualified as buried and the upper body is disqualified as floating, so no body is left to measure from.

keyTerms.meaning: Or perhaps. This introduces another possible way to see the case.
A thing lying on (or touching) something of its own kind
Buried or hidden, so it does not count as lying exposed
Floating, so it does not count as resting in its place
Measures. Here it means measuring the distance to the nearby cities for the עגלה ערופה.

steps.confusionAlert: Under this third option, neither body counts. The lower one is ruled out as buried and the upper one as floating, so no measuring is done and the עגלה ערופה would not be brought.

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִּלְמָא: מִין בְּמִינוֹ הָוֵי טָמוּן,
phrases.english: Or perhaps: a thing on its own kind counts as buried,
and a thing on its own kind also counts as floating,
and so he does not measure from the lower one
and does not measure from the upper one?
He said to him:
phrases.notes: This is אביי replying to the scholar. His answer continues on the next amud.

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: תשובה (only for the closing words 'אמר ליה', which open אביי's answer)
steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹ דִּלְמָא: מִין בְּמִינוֹ הָוֵי טָמוּן, וּמִין בְּמִינוֹ הָוֵי צָף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third possible answer to the two choices laid out in step 39, combining both of their labels at once.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a body lying on another body counts as buried, as floating, or as both. If it is both, then neither body can be the measuring point for the עגלה ערופה.
